chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from Muqarrin who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Ibn al-Kawwa' came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, [7:46] and upon the Heights there shall be men recognising all by their marks.'

So he said: 'We are upon the Heights, we recognise our helpers by their marks. We are the Recognisers through whom alone God Mighty and Majestic can be known. We are the Recognisers whom God Mighty and Majestic shall introduce on the Day of Resurrection upon the Bridge — so none shall enter Paradise except one who recognises us and whom we recognise, and none shall enter the Fire except one who denies us and whom we deny.'

Indeed, God Blessed and Exalted, had He willed, would have introduced Himself to His servants — but instead He made us His doors, His Bridge, His way and the Face through which one comes to Him. So whoever turns away from our wilayah, or prefers others over us, they shall fall off the Bridge.

They are not equal — those to whom people cling, nor where people go, to turbid springs draining into each other — and those who go to us, to clear springs flowing by the command of their Lord, neither depleting nor terminating.

key_terms.أبوابه: His doors — the Imams as the gates through which God's knowledge is accessed
key_terms.الأعراف: al-A'raf — the Heights in Quran 7:46, interpreted here as the Imams who stand as intermediaries between Paradise and Hell
key_terms.السيما: distinguishing marks or signs by which people are recognized on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الصراط: the Bridge (Sirat) — the path over which all must pass on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الولاية: wilayah — divinely-ordained guardianship and authority of the Imams
key_terms.عيون صافية: clear springs — a metaphor for the pure, inexhaustible guidance of the Imamate

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of al-A'raf (7:46) and the role of the Imams on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated via a chain ending with Muqarrin hearing Imam al-Sadiq (AS), recounts Ibn al-Kawwa's encounter with Imam Ali (AS). Ibn al-Kawwa' quoted Quran 7:46, which speaks of 'men on the Heights recognising all by their marks,' and the Imam responded that this verse refers to the Imams themselves — they are al-A'raf, the intermediaries through whom God is known. The teaching presents the Imamate as the exclusive gateway to divine knowledge: none enters Paradise without their recognition of the Imam and the Imam's recognition of them, and God made the Imams His doors, bridge, and way to Himself. The final metaphor contrasts those who follow the Imams (clear, inexhaustible springs) with those who follow others (murky, draining springs).
